title: Do social influencers affect our buying
titleChinese: 你的购买行为受 “网红” 的影响吗？
paragraphs: Have you ever been on social media and seen your favourite celebrity talking about a product? These endorsements might not be totally random, and are actually seen as a vital part of the marketing process. The question is: How do social media influencers ‘influence’ what you buy?

Human desire for status and making friends, combined with our need to belong to a group, make us susceptible to being ‘socially influenced’. Companies often use that desire to have a similar lifestyle to a celebrity we admire to hawk or launch a product. So, what do these endorsements actually do?

Firstly, they can be used to build brand awareness. A social media influencer should have a strong understanding of the platform they operate on, and therefore can create engaging content that not only adheres to the brand image, but sparks their followers’ interests in a product they might never have seen before.

Secondly, influencers can improve a company or product’s relationship with their customer base. According to InMoment’s 2018 US Retail CX Trends Report on customer loyalty, 77% of buyers have been brand loyal for more than ten years. This is also true of 60% of millennials. A popular celebrity can target key demographics and talk or blog about a product, which can create an instant and lasting bond with the consumer.

Lastly, influencers can improve customer buying habits with seemingly ‘unbiased opinions’. We are more likely to respond to ‘peer recommendation’ than traditional ads, meaning the fact we see an influencer as a ‘friend’ can make us less likely to be sceptical about what we are seeing.

So, the next time you see a celebrity talking about a product, you might want to consider that this could be a carefully crafted marketing strategy designed to target your core needs. If you find yourself perusing a product you’ve seen on social media, you may well have been influenced.

vocabulary.entry: social media /ˈsəʊʃl ˈmiːdiə/ n. 社交媒体
vocabulary.example: She spends a lot of time on social media every day.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天花很多时间在社交媒体上。

vocabulary.entry: celebrity /səˈlebrəti/ n. 名人；名流
vocabulary.example: The hotel is frequented by celebrities.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店经常有名人光顾。

vocabulary.entry: endorsement /ɪnˈdɔːsmənt/ n. 代言；认可
vocabulary.example: The brand announced a new endorsement deal with the footballer.
vocabulary.translation: 该品牌宣布与这位足球运动员达成新的代言协议。

vocabulary.entry: marketing process /ˈmɑːkɪtɪŋ ˈprəʊses/ n. 营销过程
vocabulary.example: The marketing process involves market research and product promotion.
vocabulary.translation: 营销过程包含市场调研和产品推广。

vocabulary.entry: social media influencer /ˈsəʊʃl ˈmiːdiə ˈɪnfluənsə/ n. 社交媒体网红
vocabulary.example: The social media influencer has millions of followers on Instagram.
vocabulary.translation: 这位社交媒体网红在照片墙平台上有数百万粉丝。

vocabulary.entry: status /ˈsteɪtəs/ n. 地位；身份
vocabulary.example: He cares a lot about his social status.
vocabulary.translation: 他很在意自己的社会地位。

vocabulary.entry: belong to /bɪˈlɒŋ tuː/ 属于
vocabulary.example: The book belongs to my sister.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书是我姐姐的。

vocabulary.entry: susceptible to /səˈseptəbl tuː/ 易受……影响的
vocabulary.example: Young children are more susceptible to colds.
vocabulary.translation: 幼儿更容易感冒。

vocabulary.entry: lifestyle /ˈlaɪfstaɪl/ n. 生活方式
vocabulary.example: She enjoys a healthy and active lifestyle.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢健康且积极的生活方式。

vocabulary.entry: hawk /hɔːk/ v. 推销；兜售
vocabulary.example: He was hawking cheap watches on the street corner.
vocabulary.translation: 他在街角兜售廉价手表。

vocabulary.entry: brand awareness /brænd əˈweənəs/ n. 品牌认知度
vocabulary.example: The campaign helped to increase the brand awareness among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 这场宣传活动有助于提高年轻人对该品牌的认知度。

vocabulary.entry: platform /ˈplætfɔːm/ n. 平台
vocabulary.example: This is a popular platform for online shopping.
vocabulary.translation: 这是一个很受欢迎的网购平台。

vocabulary.entry: engaging content /ɪnˈɡeɪdʒɪŋ ˈkɒntent/ n. 有吸引力的内容
vocabulary.example: The blogger creates engaging content about travel.
vocabulary.translation: 这位博主创作关于旅行的有趣内容。

vocabulary.entry: adhere to /ədˈhɪə tuː/ 遵守；符合
vocabulary.example: The design must adhere to the company's brand guidelines.
vocabulary.translation: 这个设计必须符合公司的品牌准则。

vocabulary.entry: brand image /brænd ˈɪmɪdʒ/ n. 品牌形象
vocabulary.example: The company is trying to improve its brand image.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司正努力改善自己的品牌形象。

vocabulary.entry: follower /ˈfɒləʊə/ n. 粉丝；追随者
vocabulary.example: The singer has gained thousands of new followers recently.
vocabulary.translation: 这位歌手最近新增了数千名粉丝。

vocabulary.entry: customer base /ˈkʌstəmə beɪs/ n. 客户群体
vocabulary.example: The company has built a large and loyal customer base.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司已经建立起庞大且忠诚的客户群体。

vocabulary.entry: brand loyalty /brænd ˈlɔɪəlti/ n. 品牌忠诚度
vocabulary.example: Good service can help to enhance brand loyalty.
vocabulary.translation: 优质的服务有助于提高品牌忠诚度。

vocabulary.entry: demographic /ˌdeməˈɡræfɪk/ n. 人群；人口统计群体
vocabulary.example: The product is aimed at a young demographic.
vocabulary.translation: 这款产品的目标受众是年轻人。

vocabulary.entry: bond /bɒnd/ n. 联结；纽带
vocabulary.example: There is a strong bond between the two sisters.
vocabulary.translation: 这对姐妹之间有着深厚的感情纽带。

vocabulary.entry: unbiased opinion /ʌnˈbaɪəst əˈpɪnjən/ n. 客观中立的观点
vocabulary.example: We need an unbiased opinion to settle the dispute.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要一个客观的观点来解决这场争端。

vocabulary.entry: sceptical /ˈskeptɪkl/ adj. 怀疑的
vocabulary.example: She is sceptical about the effectiveness of the new treatment.
vocabulary.translation: 她对这种新疗法的效果持怀疑态度。

sentences.english: Have you ever been on social media and seen your favourite celebrity talking about a product?
sentences.chinese: 你有没有在社交媒体上刷到过自己喜欢的名人推荐某款产品？

sentences.english: These endorsements might not be totally random, and are actually seen as a vital part of the marketing process.
sentences.chinese: 这些代言并非完全是随机之举，实际上被视为营销过程中至关重要的一环。

sentences.english: The question is: How do social media influencers ‘influence’ what you buy?
sentences.chinese: 问题来了：社交媒体网红究竟是如何“影响”你的购买决策的？

sentences.english: Human desire for status and making friends, combined with our need to belong to a group, make us susceptible to being ‘socially influenced’.
sentences.chinese: 人类对地位和交友的渴望，再加上我们渴望融入某个群体的需求，让我们很容易受到“社交影响”。

sentences.english: Companies often use that desire to have a similar lifestyle to a celebrity we admire to hawk or launch a product.
sentences.chinese: 企业常常利用这种想要拥有心仪名人同款生活方式的心理，来兜售或推销某款产品。

sentences.english: So, what do these endorsements actually do?
sentences.chinese: 那么，这些代言究竟能起到什么作用呢？

sentences.english: Firstly, they can be used to build brand awareness.
sentences.chinese: 首先，代言可以用来提升品牌认知度。

sentences.english: A social media influencer should have a strong understanding of the platform they operate on, and therefore can create engaging content that not only adheres to the brand image, but sparks their followers’ interests in a product they might never have seen before.
sentences.chinese: 社交媒体网红通常对自己运营的平台有着深刻的理解，因此能够创作出既有吸引力，又符合品牌形象的内容，同时还能激发粉丝对一款他们此前可能从未接触过的产品的兴趣。

sentences.english: Secondly, influencers can improve a company or product’s relationship with their customer base.
sentences.chinese: 其次，网红能够改善企业或产品与客户群体之间的关系。

sentences.english: According to InMoment’s 2018 US Retail CX Trends Report on customer loyalty, 77% of buyers have been brand loyal for more than ten years. This is also true of 60% of millennials.
sentences.chinese: 根据盈客洞察公司2018年发布的《美国零售客户体验趋势报告》中关于客户忠诚度的数据，77%的消费者对品牌的忠诚度可以维持十年以上，这一比例在千禧一代中也达到了60%。

sentences.english: A popular celebrity can target key demographics and talk or blog about a product, which can create an instant and lasting bond with the consumer.
sentences.chinese: 一位人气名人能够精准定位核心消费群体，通过谈论或撰写博文推荐某款产品，与消费者建立起即时且持久的联结。

sentences.english: Lastly, influencers can improve customer buying habits with seemingly ‘unbiased opinions’.
sentences.chinese: 最后，网红可以凭借看似“客观中立的观点”来影响消费者的购买习惯。

sentences.english: We are more likely to respond to ‘peer recommendation’ than traditional ads, meaning the fact we see an influencer as a ‘friend’ can make us less likely to be sceptical about what we are seeing.
sentences.chinese: 相比传统广告，我们更容易接受“同辈推荐”，这意味着当我们把网红视作“朋友”时，就不太会对他们推荐的内容产生怀疑。

sentences.english: So, the next time you see a celebrity talking about a product, you might want to consider that this could be a carefully crafted marketing strategy designed to target your core needs.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次当你再看到名人推荐产品时，不妨想一想，这或许是一个精心设计的营销策略，目的就是瞄准你的核心需求。

sentences.english: If you find yourself perusing a product you’ve seen on social media, you may well have been influenced.
sentences.chinese: 如果你发现自己正在仔细浏览某款在社交媒体上刷到的产品，那么你很可能已经被影响了。
